mountains.Name: Mountain travel
mountains.Tagline: The ranges of the Tian Shan and Pamir-Alay
mountains.Description: Most of Kyrgyzstan is mountains: peaks above seven thousand metres, glaciers, passes and high valleys that you can reach by car or on foot.

trekking.Name: Trekking
trekking.Tagline: Multi-day routes through gorges and over passes
trekking.Description: Hiking routes from day trips out of Bishkek to multi-day crossings over passes, with nights in tents, yurts and mountain huts.

culture.Name: Cultural travel
culture.Description: Yurts and felt carpets, horse games, the Manas epic, bazaars and national cuisine — everything that makes up the living culture of the country.

eco.Name: Ecotourism
eco.Tagline: Nature reserves, forests and jailoo pastures
eco.Description: Nature reserves and national parks, the walnut forests of Arslanbob, high pastures and guesthouses run by local communities (CBT).

adventure.Name: Adventure
adventure.Tagline: On horseback, by 4×4 and in border zones
adventure.Description: Horse treks, drives along mountain dirt roads, remote lakes in the border zone and expedition routes to the foot of seven-thousanders.

family.Name: Family holidays
family.Description: Issyk-Kul, warm in summer, short walks through canyons and gorges, horse rides for beginners and comfortable transfers.

history.Name: Historic sites
history.Tagline: The Great Silk Road and ancient cities
history.Description: The Tash Rabat caravanserai, Burana Tower, the mausoleums of Uzgen, the sacred Sulayman-Too mountain and petroglyphs — traces of trade routes and ancient states.

issyk-kul.Name: Issyk-Kul
issyk-kul.Tagline: A mountain sea ringed by ranges
issyk-kul.Summary: The country's largest lake at about 1,600 metres: beaches on the north shore, quiet bays on the south shore and the snowy peaks of the Terskey and Kungey Ala-Too on every side.
issyk-kul.Description:
Issyk-Kul is an endorheic high-mountain lake framed by the Kungey Ala-Too range to the north and the Terskey Ala-Too to the south. Its water is slightly salty and the lake does not freeze in winter, which explains the name — it translates as "warm lake".

The north shore with Cholpon-Ata and Bosteri is a resort coast: sandy beaches, guesthouses and promenades. The south shore is quieter and wilder: the red Skazka canyons, the Barskoon and Juuku gorges and small villages with guesthouses. At the eastern end lies Karakol, the base for hikes to Ala-Kul, Altyn-Arashan and Jeti-Oguz.

The lake combines well with mountain routes: hike up a gorge in the morning and swim at sunset in the evening.
issyk-kul.BestTime: July–August for swimming; June and September for hiking and quiet trips
Highlights: Skazka Canyon on the south shore
Sunsets over the water with the Kungey Ala-Too behind

karakol.Name: Karakol
karakol.Tagline: The trekking capital at the foot of the Terskey Ala-Too
karakol.Summary: A town at the eastern end of Issyk-Kul with the wooden Holy Trinity Church, the Dungan Mosque and trails into the Karakol, Altyn-Arashan and Jeti-Oguz valleys.
karakol.Description:
Karakol is the administrative centre of the Issyk-Kul Region and the main base for hiking in the Terskey Ala-Too. The town was founded in the second half of the 19th century, and its streets still keep single-storey houses with carved window frames.

The main sights are the wooden Holy Trinity Church and the Dungan Mosque, built without a single nail in the style of Chinese temple architecture. At the Sunday animal market you can watch horses and sheep being traded.

Karakol is the starting point for routes to Ala-Kul lake, the Altyn-Arashan hot springs and the red rocks of Jeti-Oguz, and in winter a ski base operates in the Karakol gorge.
karakol.BestTime: June–September for hiking, December–March for skiing
Highlights: Start of the trek to Ala-Kul lake

ala-kul.Name: Ala-Kul
ala-kul.Summary: A glacial lake in the Terskey Ala-Too and one of the country's best-known trekking goals. It can only be reached on foot.
ala-kul.Description:
Ala-Kul lies at the head of the Karakol valley, beneath the glaciers of the Terskey Ala-Too. The colour of the water changes from milky turquoise to deep blue depending on the weather and the light.

The classic route is the Karakol — Ala-Kul — Altyn-Arashan loop with a pass above the lake. It takes 3–4 days with nights in tents by the lake and at the Altyn-Arashan hot springs. The route requires good fitness and acclimatisation.

Mountain weather changes quickly: even in August snow is possible on the pass.
Highlights: View of the lake from the pass
Finish at the Altyn-Arashan hot springs

jeti-oguz.Name: Jeti-Oguz
jeti-oguz.Tagline: The red rocks of the Seven Bulls and the Broken Heart
jeti-oguz.Summary: A gorge with red sandstone cliffs, a resort on mineral springs and a wide jailoo pasture further up the valley.
jeti-oguz.Description:
The name Jeti-Oguz means "seven bulls" — the name of the ridge of red sandstone rocks at the entrance to the gorge. Nearby stands the Broken Heart rock, linked to several local legends.

Above the resort the valley opens into a broad pasture: in summer herders put up their yurts here and Tian Shan spruces grow on the slopes. From here hiking and horse trails lead to waterfalls and into the Kok-Jaiyk valley.

Jeti-Oguz is about 25 kilometres from Karakol and makes an easy day trip.

song-kol.Name: Song-Kol
song-kol.Tagline: A high-mountain lake and herders' summer yurts
song-kol.Summary: A lake at about 3,000 metres surrounded by endless pastures. In summer herders camp here and travellers stay in yurts.
song-kol.Description:
Song-Kol is the second largest lake in Kyrgyzstan after Issyk-Kul. It lies in an intermontane basin at about 3,000 metres, and in summer its shores become a vast pasture where herders bring herds of horses and flocks of sheep.

A night in a yurt, kumys, a horse ride along the shore and a starry sky with no light pollution are the main reasons to come to Song-Kol. You can get there by 4×4 over the passes from Kochkor, or on foot and on horseback along old herders' trails.

Nights at Song-Kol are cold even in July — bring warm clothes.
song-kol.BestTime: June to early September, when the yurt camps are open
Highlights: A night in a yurt by the shore
A horse trek to the lake

bishkek.Name: Bishkek
bishkek.Tagline: A green capital at the foot of the Kyrgyz Range
bishkek.Summary: The starting point of most trips: Ala-Too Square, the history museum, bazaars, parks and a view of the snowy range right from the city centre.
bishkek.Description:
Bishkek is the capital of Kyrgyzstan and the country's main transport hub. The city is laid out with wide avenues and boulevards, and on a clear day the snowy peaks of the Kyrgyz Ala-Too rise above it.

In the centre are Ala-Too Square with the National History Museum, the Philharmonic building, Oak Park and Erkindik Boulevard. Osh Bazaar is the place to try national food and buy dried fruit, spices and felt goods.

From Bishkek it takes about an hour to reach Ala-Archa National Park and an hour and a half to reach Burana Tower.
bishkek.BestTime: All year round; April–May and September–October are the most comfortable months
Highlights: Day trips to Ala-Archa and Burana

osh.Name: Osh
osh.Tagline: One of the oldest cities in Central Asia
osh.Summary: The southern capital of the country, with a bazaar on an old trading crossroads and the sacred Sulayman-Too mountain, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
osh.Description:
Osh is the second largest city of Kyrgyzstan, located in the Fergana Valley. The city stands on one of the branches of the Great Silk Road, and its bazaar is still one of the busiest in the region.

Above the city rises Sulayman-Too, inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2009. Its slopes hold places of pilgrimage, petroglyphs, a museum inside the mountain and viewpoints over the whole city.

Osh is a convenient base for trips to Uzgen, Lenin Peak and the Alay valley.
osh.BestTime: April–June and September–October; Osh is hot in summer

arslanbob.Name: Arslanbob
arslanbob.Tagline: A village among ancient walnut forests
arslanbob.Summary: A large village on the slopes of the Babash-Ata range surrounded by walnut forests, with two waterfalls and a well-developed network of guesthouses.
arslanbob.Description:
Arslanbob is best known for its walnut forests — among the largest natural walnut forests in the world. In autumn the villagers harvest the nuts, and whole camps of pickers appear in the forest.

Around the village are the big and small waterfalls, holy places and trails onto the slopes of the Babash-Ata range. A community-based tourism programme has long worked here: guesthouses, guides and horse rides are arranged through local residents.

Arslanbob is a good choice for unhurried ecotourism and getting to know everyday life in southern Kyrgyzstan.
arslanbob.BestTime: May–June for greenery, September–October for the walnut harvest
Highlights: Horse rides on the slopes of Babash-Ata

sary-chelek.Name: Sary-Chelek
sary-chelek.Tagline: A protected lake in the western Tian Shan
sary-chelek.Summary: A mountain lake inside a biosphere reserve, with conifer and walnut forests, several smaller lakes and a rich flora.
sary-chelek.Description:
Lake Sary-Chelek lies within the state reserve of the same name in the Chatkal range. The reserve is part of the UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves.

The steep slopes around the lake are covered with spruce, fir and broadleaf forests, and there are several smaller lakes nearby. Visits follow the reserve's rules: access to some zones is restricted.

The road to Sary-Chelek is long, so it is usually combined with Arslanbob and the Toktogul reservoir.

tash-rabat.Name: Tash Rabat
tash-rabat.Tagline: A stone caravanserai on the Silk Road
tash-rabat.Summary: A stone building in a high valley on the way to the Torugart pass — one of the country's most recognisable historic sites.
tash-rabat.Description:
Tash Rabat is a medieval stone building with domes and many small rooms, hidden in a side valley in the south of the Naryn Region. It is traditionally linked to caravan trade on one of the branches of the Great Silk Road.

It is surrounded by alpine meadows and yurt camps where you can stay overnight. From Tash Rabat a route leads over a pass to Chatyr-Kul lake, which already lies in the border zone.

The valley is high in the mountains, so it is cool here even in summer.
Highlights: A night in a yurt camp

ala-archa.Name: Ala-Archa
ala-archa.Summary: A nature park in the Kyrgyz Range with gorges, glaciers and a mountaineering camp — the most popular place for day hikes from the capital.
ala-archa.Description:
Ala-Archa National Park lies in the gorge of the river of the same name, about 40 kilometres from Bishkek. The name comes from the juniper — archa — that grows on the slopes.

Trails of different difficulty start in the park: a walk along the river, a climb to the Ak-Sai waterfall and glacier, and, for experienced mountaineers, ascents of peaks in the Kyrgyz Range.

The park charges an entrance fee; at weekends it is busy with visitors from the city.
ala-archa.BestTime: May–October for hiking, walks and skiing in winter

kel-suu.Name: Kel-Suu
kel-suu.Tagline: A fjord-like lake in the border zone
kel-suu.Summary: A long lake between sheer cliffs at the head of the Kok-Kiya valley. A border zone permit is required.
kel-suu.Description:
Kel-Suu lies in a narrow gorge of the Kokshaal-Too range, not far from the border with China. The lake stretches between almost vertical cliffs and resembles a fjord, and its water level changes noticeably over the year.

The road to the lake runs along high-altitude dirt roads of the At-Bashy district, and the last section is on foot or on horseback. The lake is in the border zone, so the permit must be arranged in advance.

This is a route for those ready for long drives and simple living in exchange for a truly remote place.

ploshchad-ala-too.Name: Ala-Too Square
ploshchad-ala-too.Summary: Bishkek's central square with a monument and the state flag.
ploshchad-ala-too.Description: The capital's main square, used for celebrations and the changing of the guard. The National History Museum and Oak Park are nearby.

nacionalnyy-istoricheskiy-muzey.Name: National History Museum
nacionalnyy-istoricheskiy-muzey.Summary: The country's main history museum on Ala-Too Square.
nacionalnyy-istoricheskiy-muzey.Description: The exhibition covers the history of Kyrgyzstan from antiquity to the present day: archaeological finds, objects of nomadic life and 20th-century documents.

bishkek-gorod.Name: Bishkek
bishkek-gorod.Summary: The capital and the starting point of most routes.
bishkek-gorod.Description: The country's main transport hub: Manas International Airport, bus stations, hotels and guesthouses.

bashnya-burana.Name: Burana Tower
bashnya-burana.Summary: An 11th-century minaret on the site of Balasagun in the Chüy valley.
bashnya-burana.Description: Burana Tower is the surviving part of a minaret on the site of a medieval city associated with Balasagun, one of the Karakhanid capitals. Nearby are stone balbal statues and a small museum. The site is part of the UNESCO World Heritage property «Silk Roads: the Routes Network of Chang'an-Tianshan Corridor».

park-ala-archa.Name: Ala-Archa National Park
park-ala-archa.Summary: A gorge with trails to the Ak-Sai waterfall and the glaciers of the Kyrgyz Range.
park-ala-archa.Description: The most accessible mountain park for residents and visitors of Bishkek. Trails start at the mountaineering camp and lead along the river, to the waterfall and to the Ak-Sai glacier.

cholpon-ata.Name: Cholpon-Ata
cholpon-ata.Summary: A resort town on the north shore of Issyk-Kul.
cholpon-ata.Description: Beaches, guesthouses, an open-air petroglyph museum and the Rukh Ordo cultural centre. The World Nomad Games were held here in 2014–2018.

rukh-ordo.Name: Rukh Ordo Cultural Centre
rukh-ordo.Summary: A museum complex on the shore of Issyk-Kul in Cholpon-Ata.
rukh-ordo.Description: A complex of chapel-pavilions, sculptures and alleys on the lakeshore dedicated to the spiritual history of Kyrgyzstan.

karakol-gorod.Name: Karakol
karakol-gorod.Summary: The regional centre and base for hikes in the Terskey Ala-Too.
karakol-gorod.Description: Hotels, guesthouses, gear rental and local guides' offices. Routes into the Karakol, Arashan and Jeti-Oguz valleys start here.

svyato-troickaya-cerkov.Name: Holy Trinity Church
svyato-troickaya-cerkov.Summary: A wooden Orthodox church in the centre of Karakol.
svyato-troickaya-cerkov.Description: A wooden church from the late 19th — early 20th century, one of Karakol's main architectural landmarks.

dunganskaya-mechet.Name: Dungan Mosque
dunganskaya-mechet.Summary: A wooden mosque in the style of Chinese temple architecture, built without nails.
dunganskaya-mechet.Description: The mosque was built by Karakol's Dungan community in the early 20th century. The wooden structure was assembled without a single nail, and its carvings and paintings recall Chinese pagodas.

dzhety-oguz-skaly.Name: Jeti-Oguz Rocks
dzhety-oguz-skaly.Summary: The red Seven Bulls and Broken Heart rocks at the entrance to the gorge.
dzhety-oguz-skaly.Description: A ridge of red sandstone rocks that gave the gorge its name. Nearby are a mineral-spring resort and trails to the Kok-Jaiyk jailoo.

ozero-ala-kul.Name: Ala-Kul Lake
ozero-ala-kul.Summary: A glacial lake at the head of the Karakol valley, reachable only on foot.
ozero-ala-kul.Description: The goal of one of the country's most popular treks. Nights are spent in tents on the shore. Acclimatisation and good fitness are required.

altyn-arashan.Name: Altyn-Arashan
altyn-arashan.Summary: Hot springs in the Arashan river valley.
altyn-arashan.Description: A small resort with hot springs, yurts and guesthouses in a high valley. People come up on foot or by 4×4; it is the finish of the loop over Ala-Kul.

kanon-skazka.Name: Skazka Canyon
kanon-skazka.Summary: Colourful clay rocks of fanciful shapes on the south shore of Issyk-Kul.
kanon-skazka.Description: A small canyon near the village of Tosor with weathered rocks in red, yellow and ochre. The best time for photos is the morning and the hours before sunset.

vodopad-barskoon.Name: Barskoon Waterfalls
vodopad-barskoon.Summary: Waterfalls in the Barskoon gorge on the south shore of the lake.
vodopad-barskoon.Description: The Barskoon gorge is known for its waterfalls and a monument to Yuri Gagarin, who holidayed here. A road to the high plateau runs through the gorge.

tamga.Name: Tamga
tamga.Summary: A quiet village on the south shore with guesthouses.
tamga.Description: A convenient overnight stop between Skazka Canyon and the Barskoon gorge. In the Tamga gorge nearby is a stone with a Tibetan inscription.

zhyrgalan.Name: Jyrgalan
zhyrgalan.Summary: A mountain village in the east of the region developing as a hub for trekking and freeride.
zhyrgalan.Description: A former mining settlement where locals opened guesthouses and marked trails. Hiking and horse routes in summer, ski touring in winter.

han-tengri.Name: Khan Tengri Peak
han-tengri.Summary: One of the most beautiful peaks of the Tian Shan, a marble pyramid where three countries meet.
han-tengri.Description: A peak in the Central Tian Shan whose marble cap glows at sunset. Base camps on the Inylchek glacier are reached by helicopter or a multi-day trek. A border zone permit is required.

ozero-son-kul.Name: Song-Kol Lake
ozero-son-kul.Summary: A high-mountain lake with summer yurt camps.
ozero-son-kul.Description: In summer herders' yurts and tourist camps stand on the shores. A night in a yurt with dinner is the main way to visit.

kochkor.Name: Kochkor
kochkor.Summary: A village famous for its shyrdak makers — the gateway to Song-Kol.
kochkor.Description: Kochkor has cooperatives where shyrdak and ala-kiyiz felt carpets are made. It is a convenient place to set off for Song-Kol over the pass.

naryn-gorod.Name: Naryn
naryn-gorod.Summary: The regional centre on the Naryn river, a stop on the way to Tash Rabat.
naryn-gorod.Description: The town stretches along the Naryn river in a narrow valley. A convenient overnight stop on the way to the south of the region.

karavan-saray-tash-rabat.Name: Tash Rabat Caravanserai
karavan-saray-tash-rabat.Summary: A medieval stone building in a mountain valley on the way to the Torugart pass.
karavan-saray-tash-rabat.Description: A building with a central dome and many rooms. Next to it are yurt camps where you can stay the night and have lunch.

ozero-chatyr-kul.Name: Chatyr-Kul Lake
ozero-chatyr-kul.Summary: A high-mountain lake near the Torugart pass in the border zone.
ozero-chatyr-kul.Description: A large lake in a high basin surrounded by ranges. It is in the border zone — a permit is required.

ozero-kel-suu.Name: Kel-Suu Lake
ozero-kel-suu.Summary: A lake between sheer cliffs in the Kokshaal-Too range.
ozero-kel-suu.Description: A remote lake in the border zone. The last part of the way is on foot or on horseback; nights are spent in a yurt camp in the valley.

osh-gorod.Name: Osh
osh-gorod.Summary: The country's southern capital in the Fergana Valley.
osh-gorod.Description: Airport, hotels and guesthouses. The starting point for trips to Uzgen, the Alay valley and Lenin Peak.

sulayman-too.Name: Sulayman-Too
sulayman-too.Summary: A sacred mountain in the centre of Osh — a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
sulayman-too.Description: A mountain with five summits, places of pilgrimage, petroglyphs and a museum inside the mountain. Inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2009.

uzgen.Name: Uzgen Architectural Complex
uzgen.Summary: A minaret and mausoleums of the Karakhanid era in the town of Uzgen.
uzgen.Description: A complex of medieval buildings: a minaret and mausoleums with rich carved decoration in fired brick and terracotta.

pik-lenina.Name: Lenin Peak
pik-lenina.Summary: A seven-thousander of the Trans-Alay range on the border with Tajikistan.
pik-lenina.Description: One of the most popular peaks above seven thousand metres among mountaineers. In summer base camps operate at the foot, on the Achik-Tash meadow, which can be reached from Osh via the Alay valley.

arslanbob-selo.Name: Arslanbob
arslanbob-selo.Summary: A village in the walnut forests with guesthouses and waterfalls.
arslanbob-selo.Description: The centre of community-based tourism in the south: guesthouses, guides, horse rides, the big and small waterfalls.

ozero-sary-chelek.Name: Sary-Chelek Lake
ozero-sary-chelek.Summary: A lake in the Sary-Chelek biosphere reserve.
ozero-sary-chelek.Description: A lake among the forested slopes of the Chatkal range. Visits follow the rules of the reserve.

toktogulskoe-vodohranilishche.Name: Toktogul Reservoir
toktogulskoe-vodohranilishche.Summary: A large reservoir among the mountains on the Bishkek — Osh highway.
toktogulskoe-vodohranilishche.Description: Turquoise water surrounded by bare mountains — a must-stop on the road between the north and the south of the country.

saymaluu-tash.Name: Saimaluu-Tash
saymaluu-tash.Summary: A high-mountain tract with thousands of rock carvings.
saymaluu-tash.Description: One of the largest concentrations of petroglyphs in Central Asia. The tract is accessible only a few months a year, on foot or on horseback.

issyk-kul-krug-3-dnya.Title: Issyk-Kul in three days: Cholpon-Ata, Karakol and Jeti-Oguz
issyk-kul-krug-3-dnya.Summary: The classic loop around the lake from the diploma example: the north shore, Karakol and the red rocks of Jeti-Oguz.
issyk-kul-krug-3-dnya.Description: A route for a first acquaintance with Issyk-Kul. On day one we drive from Bishkek along the north shore to Cholpon-Ata, visit the petroglyph museum and swim. Day two is Karakol: the Holy Trinity Church, the Dungan Mosque and lunch with ashlyan-fu. Day three starts in the Jeti-Oguz gorge by the Seven Bulls rocks, after which we return to Bishkek.
Recommendations: Bring swimwear and sunscreen
Evenings by the lake are cool — a light jacket helps
Covered clothing is required to visit the mosque

trek-ala-kul-altyn-arashan.Title: Trek to Ala-Kul Lake with a finish at Altyn-Arashan
trek-ala-kul-altyn-arashan.Summary: A four-day loop from Karakol: a climb up the gorge, a night by a turquoise lake, a pass and hot springs.
trek-ala-kul-altyn-arashan.Description: The best-known trek in Kyrgyzstan. Day one is a climb up the Karakol gorge through spruce forest to a camp by the river. Day two is a steep ascent along the waterfall to Ala-Kul lake. On day three we cross the pass above the lake and descend into the Arashan valley. The last day is rest at the hot springs and the descent to Karakol.
Recommendations: Multi-day hiking experience and good fitness are required
Spend a day or two at altitude to acclimatise
Trekking boots, a warm sleeping bag and a rain jacket are essential
Snow is possible on the pass even in August

son-kul-noch-v-yurte.Title: Song-Kol: a night in a yurt at 3,000 metres
son-kul-noch-v-yurte.Summary: A shyrdak workshop in Kochkor, the pass to Song-Kol, an evening by the yurt and a horse ride along the shore.
son-kul-noch-v-yurte.Description: A trip into nomadic Kyrgyzstan. Day one is the drive from Bishkek to Kochkor and a visit to the felt carpet makers. On day two we climb a mountain road to Song-Kol, settle into a yurt camp and go riding. Day three — sunrise over the lake and the return.
Recommendations: Nights at the lake can be near freezing — bring warm clothes
Mobile coverage on the shore is weak or absent
No riding experience is needed
Includes: Nights in a yurt and a guesthouse
Horse ride with a local guide

tash-rabat-chatyr-kul.Title: Tash Rabat and Chatyr-Kul: in the footsteps of the Silk Road
tash-rabat-chatyr-kul.Summary: Naryn, a stone caravanserai and a high-mountain lake in the border zone.
tash-rabat-chatyr-kul.Description: A route to the south of the Naryn Region. After a night in Naryn we drive to the Tash Rabat valley, explore the caravanserai and stay overnight in a yurt camp. The next day we visit Chatyr-Kul lake near the Torugart pass (the operator arranges the permit). Return via Naryn.
Recommendations: The border zone permit is arranged in advance — send your passport details to the operator
Altitude is about 3,500 m: avoid strenuous effort on the first day
Includes: Nights in a guesthouse and a yurt

ala-archa-odnodnevnyy-pohod.Title: Ala-Archa: hike to the Ak-Sai waterfall
ala-archa-odnodnevnyy-pohod.Summary: A day trip from Bishkek to the national park with a climb to the waterfall.
ala-archa-odnodnevnyy-pohod.Description: In the morning we leave Bishkek and an hour later reach the entrance to Ala-Archa National Park. The climb to the Ak-Sai waterfall takes a few hours; lunch is in a clearing by the river. In the evening we return to the city.
Recommendations: Bring comfortable shoes with good grip and water
The park is busy at weekends — we leave early

burana-za-odin-den.Title: Burana Tower: the Chüy valley in one day
burana-za-odin-den.Summary: A short trip from Bishkek to the 11th-century minaret, the balbals and the site museum.
burana-za-odin-den.Description: An easy trip available all year round. We explore Burana Tower, climb to its viewing platform, walk through the field of stone statues and visit the small site museum.
Recommendations: The stairs inside the tower are narrow — bring a torch
Suitable for families with children

arslanbob-sary-chelek.Title: The walnut forests of Arslanbob and Sary-Chelek Lake
arslanbob-sary-chelek.Summary: The south of the country: Osh, Arslanbob guesthouses, waterfalls and a protected lake.
arslanbob-sary-chelek.Description: The route starts in Osh with a walk on Sulayman-Too. Then we go to Arslanbob, stay in a guesthouse, walk in the walnut forest and climb to the waterfall. From here we head to the Sary-Chelek reserve and spend a day by the lake. The way back runs past the Toktogul reservoir.
Recommendations: The reserve has visiting rules — follow the rangers' instructions
Autumn is walnut-picking season in Arslanbob

osh-uzgen.Title: Osh and Uzgen: ancient cities of the south
osh-uzgen.Summary: The sacred Sulayman-Too mountain, Osh Bazaar and the Karakhanid mausoleums of Uzgen.
osh-uzgen.Description: Day one is devoted to Osh: the climb up Sulayman-Too, the museum in the mountain's cave and a walk through the bazaar. Day two is a trip to Uzgen to see the 11th–12th-century minaret and mausoleums, then back to Osh.
Recommendations: It is hot in summer — plan walks for the morning and evening
Covered clothing is required at holy sites

yuzhnyy-bereg-skazka-barskoon.Title: The south shore: Skazka Canyon and the Barskoon waterfalls
yuzhnyy-bereg-skazka-barskoon.Summary: A relaxed trip along the south shore of Issyk-Kul with walks for the whole family.
yuzhnyy-bereg-skazka-barskoon.Description: From Bishkek we go to the south shore of Issyk-Kul, walk among the colourful rocks of Skazka Canyon and spend the night in a guesthouse in Tamga. On day two we go up the Barskoon gorge to the waterfalls and return.
Recommendations: There is little shade in the canyon — bring a hat and water
Suitable for children aged 6 and over

kel-suu-ekspediciya.Title: Kel-Suu: an expedition to a lake in the border zone
kel-suu-ekspediciya.Summary: A long drive via Naryn and At-Bashy, a yurt camp in Kok-Kiya and a walk out to the lake between the cliffs.
kel-suu-ekspediciya.Description: A route for those who want to see one of the most remote lakes in the country. Day one is the drive to Naryn. Day two follows dirt roads into the Kok-Kiya valley with a night in yurts. Day three is a hike or horse ride to Kel-Suu lake. Day four is the return.
Recommendations: The border zone permit is arranged in advance
Long off-road drives — keep this in mind if you get motion sick
There is no mobile coverage in the valley

chto-posmotret-v-kyrgyzstane.Title: What to see in Kyrgyzstan: 10 places for a first trip
chto-posmotret-v-kyrgyzstane.Lead: Lakes at three thousand metres, red rocks, a Silk Road caravanserai and a sacred mountain in the middle of a city — a short list for first-time visitors.
chto-posmotret-v-kyrgyzstane.Body:
Kyrgyzstan is small, but very diverse. In two weeks you can see high-mountain lakes, glaciers, walnut forests and ancient cities — if you plan the route well.

## The north: Bishkek, Ala-Archa and Burana

Most trips begin in Bishkek. On the first day walk across Ala-Too Square and visit the National History Museum, and on the next day go to Ala-Archa National Park. An hour and a half to the east is Burana Tower, an 11th-century minaret on the site of a medieval city.

## Issyk-Kul and Karakol

Issyk-Kul is the country's main lake. The north shore suits a beach holiday, the south shore — walks through Skazka Canyon and the gorges. On the eastern shore stands Karakol with the wooden Holy Trinity Church, the Dungan Mosque and the start of many treks.

## Ala-Kul and Jeti-Oguz

Ala-Kul lake is the goal of a multi-day hike, while the red rocks of Jeti-Oguz can be seen on a single trip from Karakol.

## Song-Kol and Tash Rabat

In the centre of the country lies the high Song-Kol, where herders live in summer and yurt camps operate. Further south, on the way to the Torugart pass, is the stone caravanserai of Tash Rabat.

## The south: Osh, Uzgen and Arslanbob

Osh is one of the oldest cities in the region, with Sulayman-Too mountain on the UNESCO World Heritage List. Nearby are the mausoleums of Uzgen and the walnut forests of Arslanbob.

## How to fit it all in

In a week you can drive the northern loop: Bishkek — Issyk-Kul — Karakol — Song-Kol. The south needs another week or a domestic flight to Osh. You can build your own route and see an estimated cost right away in the TurMax planner.

kuda-poehat-letom.Title: Where to go in summer: high lakes and jailoo pastures
kuda-poehat-letom.Lead: Summer is when the passes open, herders move up to the jailoo and yurt camps welcome guests. Here is where to go in June, July and August.
kuda-poehat-letom.Body:
The mountain season in Kyrgyzstan is short: many high roads and trails are open roughly from June to September. It is better to plan your trip in advance.

## June: green valleys

In June the valleys are still green while snow may remain on the passes. It is a good time for Ala-Archa, Jeti-Oguz, Arslanbob and drives along Issyk-Kul without the summer crowds.

## July: the high country and yurts open

By July yurt camps start operating at Song-Kol and in the Tash Rabat valley. The trail to Ala-Kul lake opens and the season for climbing seven-thousanders begins.

## August: the warm water of Issyk-Kul

In August the water of Issyk-Kul is at its warmest, and the north shore is at the peak of the beach season. It is the most popular month for travel, so book accommodation and transport early.

## What to bring

Even in summer it can be close to freezing at night at 3,000 metres. You will need a warm jacket, a hat, sunscreen and sunglasses — the mountain sun is very strong.

samye-krasivye-ozera.Title: The most beautiful lakes of Kyrgyzstan
samye-krasivye-ozera.Lead: Issyk-Kul, Song-Kol, Ala-Kul, Sary-Chelek, Kel-Suu and Chatyr-Kul — six lakes worth a trip to the mountains.
samye-krasivye-ozera.Body:
Kyrgyzstan has thousands of lakes, most of them high-mountain and glacial. Here are six that most often appear in travellers' itineraries.

## Issyk-Kul

The country's largest lake, at about 1,600 metres. In summer — beaches and swimming; the rest of the year — views of snowy ranges from both shores.

## Song-Kol

The second largest lake, at about 3,000 metres. The main reasons to go are herders' yurts, horses and the starry sky.

## Ala-Kul

A turquoise glacial lake above Karakol, reachable only on foot. The goal of one of the country's most popular treks.

## Sary-Chelek

A lake in a biosphere reserve in the west of the country, surrounded by conifer and broadleaf forests.

## Kel-Suu

A lake between sheer cliffs in the border zone near the Chinese border. A permit and readiness for off-road driving are required.

## Chatyr-Kul

A high-mountain lake near the Torugart pass. It is usually combined with a trip to Tash Rabat.

nacionalnaya-kuhnya.Title: National cuisine: what to try in Kyrgyzstan
nacionalnaya-kuhnya.Lead: Beshbarmak, plov, lagman, kumys and boorsok — a guide to the dishes you will meet in a yurt, a guesthouse and at the bazaar.
nacionalnaya-kuhnya.Body:
Kyrgyz cuisine grew out of nomadic life: lots of meat, dairy and dough. In the south Uzbek cuisine has a noticeable influence, in Karakol — Dungan cuisine.

## Beshbarmak

The main festive dish: boiled meat with thinly cut noodles and broth. The name means "five fingers" — it was traditionally eaten by hand.

## Plov and lagman

In the south, especially in Osh, plov is cooked in a kazan over an open fire. Lagman — hand-pulled noodles with meat and vegetables — is popular all over the country.

## Ashlyan-fu

A cold spicy soup with starch noodles — the signature dish of Karakol, which came from Dungan cuisine.

## Kumys and dairy products

In summer herders on the jailoo make kumys from mare's milk. It is worth trying at least once, but carefully if you are not used to fermented milk drinks.

## Boorsok and tea

Boorsok are small pieces of fried dough served with tea in almost every home.

kultura-i-tradicii.Title: Culture and traditions: the yurt, kok-boru and the Manas epic
kultura-i-tradicii.Lead: How a yurt is built, why horse games fill whole stadiums and what Manas means for Kyrgyz culture.
kultura-i-tradicii.Body:
Despite the rapid growth of cities, nomadic traditions remain part of everyday life in Kyrgyzstan — especially in summer, when families move up to the pastures.

## The yurt

A yurt is a collapsible dwelling with a wooden frame and felt covering. It can be assembled in a few hours and carried on horses. The knowledge and skills of making Kyrgyz and Kazakh yurts are inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage. The image of the yurt's crown — the tunduk — appears on the national flag of Kyrgyzstan.

## Felt: shyrdak and ala-kiyiz

A shyrdak is a mosaic felt carpet made of sewn pieces; an ala-kiyiz is a pressed felt carpet with a pattern. In the village of Kochkor there are workshops where you can watch the process and buy carpets.

## Kok-boru and horse games

Kok-boru is a team horse game in which riders fight for a goat carcass and throw it into the opponents' "kazan". Horse games are an essential part of festivals, and the World Nomad Games have been held three times in Cholpon-Ata.

## The Manas epic

Manas is a heroic epic about the hero Manas and his descendants, one of the longest epics in the world. It is performed by storytellers called manaschy, and hearing a live performance is a special experience.

sovety-puteshestvennikam.Title: Travel tips: season, altitude, permits and connectivity
sovety-puteshestvennikam.Lead: Practical things to think about before your trip: acclimatisation, border zones, roads and mobile coverage in the mountains.
sovety-puteshestvennikam.Body:
The mountains make travelling in Kyrgyzstan impressive, but they require preparation. Here is what to know in advance.

## Altitude and acclimatisation

Many popular places lie above 3,000 metres: Song-Kol, Tash Rabat, Ala-Kul. Climb gradually, drink more water and do not plan heavy exertion on your first day at altitude. A headache and shortness of breath are a reason to slow down, and a sharp deterioration in how you feel is a reason to descend.

## Border zones

Part of the territory near the borders — for example the area of Kel-Suu and Chatyr-Kul lakes and the Inylchek valley — is in the border zone. A permit is required and must be arranged in advance. TurMax route cards mark such places.

## Roads

The main highways are paved, but many lakes and gorges are reached by gravel and dirt roads. Travel times on them are much longer than they look on the map. The TurMax route planner takes the road type into account and warns you if a day has more than 8 hours on the road.

## Connectivity and offline maps

In the high mountains there is often no mobile signal. Download offline maps and save your route as GPX — it opens in a navigation app without the internet.

## Money

Cities have ATMs and card payments, but villages and yurt camps more often accept cash in som.
